newsitem.title: USA: Voters okay $94.5 mln Tulsa, Okla., school bond.
newsitem.headline: Voters okay $94.5 mln Tulsa, Okla., school bond.

text.p: Voters in Tulsa, Okla., Independent School District No. 1 approved four bond proposals totalling $94.5 millon Tuesday, a spokeswoman for the district said Wednesday.
"We had about 58,700 voters, and the four issues all passed," said Anna Brown, the district's coordinator of publications.

Though still unofficial, early results show that 68 percent of those voting approved a $54.5 million building renovation bond proposal, Brown said. The proposal includes plans to build a new elementary school to replace the district's oldest functioning building. Yes votes totaled 40,070, while no votes totaled 18,699.
Sixty-seven percent of those who voted passed a $10 million library proposal, with 39,502 voters for it and 19,119 against it.

The $25 million classroom materials and equipment bond issue also passed with 67 percent in favor. Yes votes totaled 38,902 while naysayers totaled 19,552. The $5 million school bus replacement bond proposal got the nod from 64 percent of those voting, with 37,314 in favor and 21,130 opposed.
The proposed $94.5 million sale still needs approval from the state attorney general, Brown said.
